title: Driver captured in Medellín after trying to bribe traffic officer
seoTitle: Driver captured in Medellín after bribery attempt
subtitle: On August 10, 2026, a driver tried to pay to avoid a fine and ended up assaulting the officer, being arrested by police
excerpt: On August 10, 2026, a driver was detained in Medellín after offering money to a traffic officer, brushing him and physically assaulting him, leading to a lawsuit.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On August 10, 2026, a driver was detained in Medellín after trying to bribe and assault a traffic officer during an irregular parking control on Avenue 33. The incident prompted police intervention and action by the Mobility Secretariat.

Driving and bribery attempt

The officer found a Mercedes-Benz GLC parked on the public road and requested the owner's documentation. The driver offered money to the officer intending to avoid issuing a ticket.

Assault on the traffic officer

When the proposal was rejected, the officer became the target of a physical assault: the driver allegedly brushed and struck the officer. The incident was captured on video, showing part of the violence.

Police intervention and arrest

The officer requested support from the Metropolitan Police, which arrived on the scene and arrested the driver. The suspect was handed over to the National General Prosecutor's Office to answer for the acts committed.

Legal procedures and possible penalty

The driver faces a charge of violence against a public servant, a crime that can carry a sentence of 4 to 8 years in prison. The traffic officer received medical attention and filed a criminal complaint.

Reaction of the Mobility Secretariat

Medellín's Mobility Secretary, Pablo Ruiz, condemned the assault and the alleged bribery, stating that the administration will not tolerate violence against employees. "Our agents work daily to protect your life and integrity, preserve order and the roads, and guarantee mobility. The duty as citizens is to respect and obey traffic rules and responsibly assume our behavior on the road," he said.

With this case, the number of people captured in 2026 for assaults on traffic officers in the city rises to 12, according to the Mobility Secretariat.

With information from El Colombiano.
